hints: Look closely at what the molecule really is, one molecule has 2 Al atoms and 6 Cl atoms, so think in terms of $\text{Al}_2\text{Cl}_6$.
Remember one mole of molecules contains $6.02 \times 10^{23}$ molecules, so multiply by 2 for aluminium atoms and by 6 for chlorine atoms.
Also recall chlorine has isotopes and empirical means simplest ratio, then check which statement survives both ideas.
walkthrough:
**Find the molecular formula**

Great start, let's translate words into chemistry. Two Al atoms and six Cl atoms per molecule means the molecular formula is:
$$\text{Al}_2\text{Cl}_6$$

**Remember chlorine has isotopes**

Chlorine exists naturally as $^{35}\text{Cl}$ and $^{37}\text{Cl}$. So in any 1 g sample, the Cl atoms do not all have identical mass. This already tells us to be careful with statement A.

**Use Avogadro's number for atoms per mole**

One mole of $\text{Al}_2\text{Cl}_6$ contains $6.02 \times 10^{23}$ molecules.

Number of Al atoms = $2 \times 6.02 \times 10^{23} = 1.20 \times 10^{24}$
$$\text{Number of Cl atoms} = 6 \times 6.02 \times 10^{23} = 3.61 \times 10^{24}$$

**Check empirical versus molecular formula**

Empirical means simplest whole number ratio. Divide $\text{Al}_2\text{Cl}_6$ by 2 to get:
$$\text{Empirical formula} = \text{AlCl}_3$$
So $\text{Al}_2\text{Cl}_6$ is molecular, not empirical. Putting it all together, only the chlorine atom count matches.

options.A: Incorrect. Chlorine has two common isotopes, $^{35}\text{Cl}$ and $^{37}\text{Cl}$, with different masses. Any sample of 1 g will contain a mixture, so not all Cl atoms have the same mass.
options.B: Incorrect. One mole contains $6.02 \times 10^{23}$ molecules of $\text{Al}_2\text{Cl}_6$, but each molecule has 2 Al atoms. So Al atoms = $2 \times 6.02 \times 10^{23} = 1.20 \times 10^{24}$, not $6.02 \times 10^{23}$. This trap forgets to multiply by 2.
options.C: Correct. Each $\text{Al}_2\text{Cl}_6$ molecule has 6 Cl atoms. One mole gives $6 \times 6.02 \times 10^{23} = 3.61 \times 10^{24}$ chlorine atoms, which matches exactly.
options.D: Incorrect. $\text{Al}_2\text{Cl}_6$ is the molecular formula. The empirical formula is the simplest ratio, $\text{AlCl}_3$, obtained by dividing by 2. Students often confuse molecular and empirical formulas here.
